steps.title: Delicate and savoury
steps.body: Garganega gives light to medium-bodied whites with lemon, pear, white peach, almond, white flowers and a saline, mineral edge. Acidity is medium to high. It's the main grape of Soave, in the Veneto. With age, it gains honey and nutty notes.

steps.title: An old Veneto grape
steps.body: Garganega is one of Italy's oldest white grapes, recorded around Verona since the 13th century. DNA shows it's identical to Sicily's Grecanico and related to many central Italian grapes, like Trebbiano Toscano. It's vigorous and late-ripening; yields must be controlled for quality.

steps.prompt: What is Garganega called in Sicily?
steps.explanation: DNA shows Garganega and Grecanico are the same grape.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon colour, lemon and almond, a light floral note, and a crisp, slightly saline palate with a bitter almond finish. Better Soave has more body and texture. Compared with Pinot Grigio, Garganega has more almond and minerality.

steps.prompt: Garganega is the main grape of Soave.
steps.explanation: Yes. Soave must be at least 70% Garganega.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Garganega gives lemon, almond and a mineral edge
It's an old Veneto grape, identical to Grecanico
It's the main grape of Soave
